source_documents.title: Deep-blue solid-state emission from Ternaphthalene: Photophysical tuning via multi-chromophore architectures

reference_evidence_units.quote: Kinetic analysis revealed that this efficiency stems from the significant suppression of non-radiative rates (knr) due to the restricted intramolecular rotation in the rigid crystal lattice.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TNps
reference_evidence_units.statement: High solid-state yields come from lower knr as the crystal restricts ring rotation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No viscosity or low-temperature test in solution.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Furthermore, a decisive topological effect on the radiative rate (kf) was demonstrated.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TNps
reference_evidence_units.statement: kf depends on the naphthalene connectivity.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This negligible solvatochromic shift indicates that the lowest excited singlet state (S1) possesses a locally excited (LE) nature rather than intra molecular charge transfer (ICT) character.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TNps
reference_evidence_units.statement: No solvatochromism: LE, not ICT, emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This suggests that the twisted multichromophore architecture effectively suppresses the formation of nonemissive H-aggregates, thereby preventing complete fluorescence quenching (ACQ) commonly observed in planar polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TNps

reference_evidence_units.quote: intramolecular rotation (RIR) mechanism, placing TNps within the framework of crystallization-induced emission enhancement (CIEE), rather than aggregation-induced emission in amorphous states.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TNps
reference_evidence_units.statement: Solid-state gains are assigned to RIR (CIEE).

reference_evidence_units.quote: Collec tively, these calculations demonstrate that while the multi-chromophore scaffold ensures high singlet energy (deep-blue emission), the specific topology of the naphthalene connectivities (1,4-, 1,5- and 2,6- vs. 2,7-) acts as a decisive switch for the radiative probability.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TNps
reference_evidence_units.statement: Connectivity controls the S1 oscillator strength.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This theoretical result aligns perfectly with the experimentally observed large radiative rates (kf ~ 5 × 108 s− 1), confirming the allowed nature of the π-π* transition.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1,4-, 1,5-, 2,6-TNps

reference_evidence_units.quote: In sharp contrast, the derivatives based on the 2,7-naphthalene linkage (2711, 2712 and 2722) display drastically different electronic features.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2,7-TNps
reference_evidence_units.statement: 2,7-linked TNps have very small f; kf 0.2-0.5e8 s-1 and τf 11-13 ns.

reference_evidence_units.quote: These results lead to the conclusion that the dramatic variation in fluorescence lifetimes observed in the TNp series—spanning from nanoseconds to tens of nanoseconds—is governed not by external factors such as aggregation or solvation, but predominantly by the internal molecular topology (1,4-, 1,5- and 2,6- vs. 2,7-connectivity).
reference_evidence_units.subject: TNps

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: knr drops from 0.6e8 to 0.3e8 s-1 in the crystal (Φf 0.94), which the abstract assigns to restricted intramolecular rotation (CIEE).

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Allowed S1 transition with kf 5.6e8 s-1 (Φf 0.90 in CHCl3); the abstract's topological effect on kf.

environment_context: twisted structure suppresses H-aggregate (ACQ) quenching in the solid (E04)

contrast_group.varied_factor: connectivity of the central naphthalene (2,6 vs 2,7) with two 1-naphthyl wings
contrast_group.paper_difference: 2611 has an allowed S1 transition (kf 5.6e8 s-1, τf 1.6 ns); 2711 is nearly forbidden (kf 0.5e8 s-1, τf 13.2 ns).

basis: compound code 2611 (2,6-linked central naphthalene, two 1-naphthyl wings)
